title: AZ-900 · Describe Azure networking services · Module assessment

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure networking services
questions.question: Which statement best describes Azure Virtual Network (VNet)?

options.text: A private network in Azure that enables resources to communicate securely with each other and with external networks
Redundant connectivity at ExpressRoute peering locations for higher availability
A subdivision of a virtual network address space used to segment resources
Managing domain records through the portal, PowerShell, CLI, REST API, or SDKs

questions.explanation: Azure Virtual Network (VNet) is a private network in Azure that enables resources to communicate securely with each other and with external networks.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure networking services
questions.question: In the context of this Microsoft Learn unit, what does Subnet refer to?

options.text: An encrypted tunnel that carries trusted private-network traffic across an untrusted network such as the internet
A configuration in which both gateway instances can carry traffic using separate public IP addresses and tunnels
A private connection between VNets that uses the Microsoft backbone instead of the public internet
A subdivision of a virtual network address space used to segment resources

questions.explanation: Subnet is a subdivision of a virtual network address space used to segment resources.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure networking services
questions.question: Which description correctly matches Public endpoint?

options.text: The default resiliency configuration in which a standby VPN gateway instance can take over during failure
The private connectivity path used to connect a site to Microsoft cloud services
A feature that connects on-premises sites to each other through their ExpressRoute circuits and the Microsoft backbone
An endpoint with a public IP address that can be reachable from the internet

questions.explanation: Public endpoint is an endpoint with a public IP address that can be reachable from the internet.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure networking services
questions.question: Which of the following is the best definition of Private endpoint?

options.text: A resource containing inbound and outbound rules that allow or deny network traffic
Routing DNS queries to a nearby available Azure DNS server for performance and resiliency
An endpoint with a private IP address inside a virtual network
Role-based permissions applied through Azure Resource Manager to control DNS resource management

questions.explanation: Private endpoint is an endpoint with a private IP address inside a virtual network.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure networking services
questions.question: What is the primary meaning of Network security group (NSG) in Azure fundamentals?

options.text: The private connectivity path used to connect a site to Microsoft cloud services
An encrypted tunnel that carries trusted private-network traffic across an untrusted network such as the internet
A resource containing inbound and outbound rules that allow or deny network traffic
An endpoint with a public IP address that can be reachable from the internet

questions.explanation: Network security group (NSG) is a resource containing inbound and outbound rules that allow or deny network traffic.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure networking services
questions.question: Select the TWO statements that are correct according to this unit.

options.text: Azure Virtual Network (VNet): an endpoint with a private IP address inside a virtual network.
Azure Virtual Network (VNet): a private network in Azure that enables resources to communicate securely with each other and with external networks.
Subnet: a private connection between VNets that uses the Microsoft backbone instead of the public internet.
Subnet: a subdivision of a virtual network address space used to segment resources.
Public endpoint: an encrypted tunnel that carries trusted private-network traffic across an untrusted network such as the internet.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Azure Virtual Network (VNet) — a private network in Azure that enables resources to communicate securely with each other and with external networks; and Subnet — a subdivision of a virtual network address space used to segment resources.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure networking services
questions.question: Which TWO statements accurately reflect the concepts covered in this unit?

options.text: Public endpoint: a custom route used to control traffic flow between subnets or virtual networks.
Public endpoint: an endpoint with a public IP address that can be reachable from the internet.
Private endpoint: an endpoint with a private IP address inside a virtual network.
Private endpoint: a specialized VM that performs network functions such as firewalling or WAN optimization.
Private endpoint: a virtual network gateway used to create encrypted connectivity between Azure and other networks or devices.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Public endpoint — an endpoint with a public IP address that can be reachable from the internet; and Private endpoint — an endpoint with a private IP address inside a virtual network.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure networking services
questions.question: Select TWO correct statements about the material in this Microsoft Learn unit.

options.text: Network security group (NSG): a mechanism that provides optimized and secure connectivity from a VNet to supported Azure services.
Network security group (NSG): a resource containing inbound and outbound rules that allow or deny network traffic.
Network security group (NSG): a VPN connection between an on-premises network gateway and an Azure virtual network.
User-defined route (UDR): a virtual network gateway used to create encrypted connectivity between Azure and other networks or devices.
User-defined route (UDR): a custom route used to control traffic flow between subnets or virtual networks.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Network security group (NSG) — a resource containing inbound and outbound rules that allow or deny network traffic; and User-defined route (UDR) — a custom route used to control traffic flow between subnets or virtual networks.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure networking services
questions.question: Which TWO statements are consistent with the unit content?

options.text: Service endpoint: a VPN connection from an individual client device to an Azure virtual network.
Service endpoint: a mechanism that provides optimized and secure connectivity from a VNet to supported Azure services.
Virtual network peering: a private connection between VNets that uses the Microsoft backbone instead of the public internet.
Virtual network peering: an encrypted tunnel that carries trusted private-network traffic across an untrusted network such as the internet.
User-defined route (UDR): a VPN connection from an individual client device to an Azure virtual network.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Virtual network peering — a private connection between VNets that uses the Microsoft backbone instead of the public internet; and Service endpoint — a mechanism that provides optimized and secure connectivity from a VNet to supported Azure services.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure networking services
questions.question: Choose the TWO accurate statements.

options.text: Virtual private network (VPN): an encrypted tunnel that carries trusted private-network traffic across an untrusted network such as the internet.
Network virtual appliance: a VPN connection between an on-premises network gateway and an Azure virtual network.
Network virtual appliance: a specialized VM that performs network functions such as firewalling or WAN optimization.
Virtual network peering: a VPN connection between virtual networks.
Virtual private network (VPN): a VPN model that uses routing to determine which traffic enters encrypted tunnels and is preferred for many modern scenarios.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Network virtual appliance — a specialized VM that performs network functions such as firewalling or WAN optimization; and Virtual private network (VPN) — an encrypted tunnel that carries trusted private-network traffic across an untrusted network such as the internet.
